notes: v217 — PAY-CARD-ROLE + PREFS-ROLE-SPLIT + PNL-REVENUE-RATE + AUTOSTART-DRIVER-ONLY (owner rulings over his own screens, Oct 21, 2026 15:29–15:34 MDT). (1) PAY-CARD-ROLE (15:29 — 'I thought I told you we don't have driver pay/owner pay... Owner revenue is based on the job!?'): the Preferences Pay card carried BOTH a global Client billing rate and a Driver wage rate — the abolished split, and a global rate contradicting rates-on-the-job. The billing field is OFF every face (owner-operator, driver, office, Fleet Manager alike); the Pay card keeps only the user's own pay facts — payment standard, travel bonus, and MY wage, relabelled 'Your wage rate' on the owner-operator face (it is his own wage — the one every driver sets for himself and that travels via Connect to post as his cost on the boss's books). Billing rates live where the law puts them: on the job (Dispatch job rates; a customer's last rate is remembered as the default for their next job). MIGRATION (hard requirement): the stored global billingRate is never written or deleted by Preferences anymore — it survives as the company fallback default wherever a job/customer has no rate of its own yet, so every existing user's numbers price exactly as before. (2) PREFS-ROLE-SPLIT (15:30, over the Dave Cooper office account — 'This suppose to be only a driver setting'): the whole Truck card (truck number, load/trailer type, odometer field + photo buttons, safety sticker, fuel-economy unit, daily-odometer-photos toggle) renders ONLY for users who drive (driver + both), gated on the same drives-answer that gates the tracker and PTI; office-only accounts never render it, and the Save handler guards those writes the v76 way so an office save completes and keeps whatever is stored. Business/office facts (invoice number, the tax-includes-rate in the Company card) are not driver settings and stay for all roles. (3) PNL-REVENUE-RATE (15:33, over P&L Monthly analysis — 'This revenue is not 93 x by my hours'): his October revenue read $4,843.00 over 167.0h — priced at his WAGE ($29) — because the analysis's revenue leg summed his days' paid (wage-priced) totals. The revenue leg now prices each day's hours at the CLIENT rate — the day's own job rate first (the dispatch record, v173), the stored company rate second (the migrated fallback) — for own days; crew days already priced from the pipe at the client rate and still do. The salaries leg keeps reading the wage-priced lines untouched. His October now reads revenue $15,531.00 (167.0 x $93), salaries $4,843.00 (167.0 x $29) — the acceptance fixture, pinned in the new suite along with job-rate-wins, no-rate parity (a book with no client rate anywhere is byte-identical to before), and source separation (moving the client rate moves revenue only; moving the wage moves salaries only). ConnectPipe.pricingFor lost its wage fallbacks the same hour: the crew client rate is the stored company rate ALONE, so with no company rate on file crew revenue is honestly unpriced instead of wage-priced — a wage value never reaches a revenue multiplication. The dispatch completion money plan (v52 lineage, jobRate already wins inside it) is untouched, as are invoice/pay-stub building (wage chain) — the read-path audit: pricingFor CHANGED (wage fallbacks out); completion settings STAYED (brief-protected); the Preferences writer REMOVED (stored value survives); invoice/revenue/chatbot carry no billing read. The Dispatch crew board's unpriced-revenue hint no longer sends the user to the removed Preferences field. (4) AUTOSTART-DRIVER-ONLY (15:34 — 'Auto start is an option for the driver'): Revenue's Auto-start button + settings card were already role-gated in code (the v76 lineage — the panel and button render only when App.userRole() is not office); the sighting traced to that device's account role reading non-office (the profile bleed v216 fixed). No code change — the gate is now pinned by suite so it cannot regress, placement exactly where v201 put it. New suite tools/pay-card-role-test.js (62 assertions: every face's Pay card, the Truck gate + office-save survival of truck/safety/billing data, the October fixture worlds, crew pricing at 93/29 plus the no-rate honesty case, the Revenue gate for office/driver/both). Superseded pins updated with the rulings cited in place: preferences-v137, preferences-live-v149 (its v149 office door section rewritten as the migration proof), preferences-repaint-v161, invoice-format, queue-v163 (the v163 wage-label pin). Standing pin move 216 -> 217 across index.html and the test files. PARKED BY NAME, NOT BUILT: CREW-RATE-DOOR — a brand-new payer account with no stored company rate now has no in-app door to set the crew-pricing fallback (job rates cover the owner's own dispatches; the stored value still arrives via setup-era data) — a design call for the owner. Ships as webVersion 217.
